script.title: Methods of Arm's Length Price
script.caption_hook: Related companies deal with each other. So who decides the fair price?

lines.say: Ma'am, how do we price a deal between two related companies?
Price it like strangers would. Arm's length price is what two unrelated parties would agree on.
But when does it apply? Any two companies?
Only between associated enterprises. That means international transactions, and certain specified domestic transactions.
And how do we find that price?
The Act gives six methods. Five are named, plus any other method prescribed by the CBDT.
Do we try CUP first, always?
No. There's no order. Choose the most appropriate method on facts, comparability and data available.
Okay, so what does RPM do? Give an example.
Distributor resells for ₹10,000. Normal gross margin is 20% of resale price, ₹2,000. No customs duty assumed. ALP is ₹8,000.
Oh! So RPM uses gross margin. What about the others?
TNMM compares net profit margin against a base. CPM uses cost plus gross mark-up. PSM splits combined profit by contribution.
Remember: pick the method by facts, not by habit.

check_notes: Checker: Line 4 (voice) and its board: "Only between associated enterprises" is wrong as a rule. Under section 92B(1), an international transaction is one between two or more associated enterprises where at least one is a non-resident. However, section 92B(2) treats a transaction with an unrelated person as a deemed international transaction when a prior agreement or arrangement with an associated enterprise sets its terms. Specified domestic transactions under section 92BA are defined by the transactions listed there (for example, those under sections 80A and 80-IA(8)/(10)), not by associated-enterprise status. Correct version: "ALP applies to international transactions between associated enterprises (including deemed international transactions under section 92B(2)) and to specified domestic transactions under section 92BA." The board should not show 'Associated enterprises' as a separate third item next to the two kinds of transaction. Use 'International transactions (AEs, at least one non-resident)' and 'Specified domestic transactions (s. 92BA)'.

Checker: Line 10 (RPM example), minor: the example doesn't say the goods were bought from an associated enterprise and resold to an unrelated party. Add this, for example: "Goods bought from an AE are resold to an unrelated buyer for ₹10,000". The arithmetic is correct: ₹10,000 − 20% gross margin of ₹2,000 = ₹8,000, with no customs duty or other purchase costs.
reviewer_note: Corrected: six methods (five named plus prescribed other method, Rule 10AB); scope includes specified domestic transactions; RPM margin stated as 20% of resale price with no purchase expenses assumed (₹10,000 − ₹2,000 = ₹8,000). Please verify word count is within 120-175.
